paths.notes: OAuth providers, token storage, service-account impersonation

evidence.claim: Every declarative tool is a BaseDeclarativeTool that validates parameters against a JSON schema before returning a ToolInvocation.
ToolRegistry owns model-facing function declarations and injects a synthetic wait_for_previous parameter into every declaration.
Plan-mode gating and excluded-tools filtering occur at declaration time inside ToolRegistry, not inside tools.
Config.createToolRegistry is the canonical registration site for built-ins; each tool class is gated by Config.getCoreTools().
DiscoveredToolInvocation runs as a spawned subprocess with 10MB stdout/stderr byte budgets and treats any non-empty stderr as failure.
MCP tool names are fully qualified as mcp_<server>_<tool>, sanitized to [a-zA-Z0-9_.:-], and truncated to 63 chars with a '...' middle marker.
MCP server discovery obeys three independent gates: admin allow/block, user enablement, and folder trust.
Per-server tool filtering applies excludeTools before includeTools; allowlists intersect while blocklists union on config merge.
MCP tool invocations emit progress tokens and map SDK-transport failures into MCP-spec 'isError:true' responses rather than throwing.
BaseToolInvocation.shouldConfirmExecute short-circuits in AUTO_EDIT mode for edit/write tools via respectsAutoEdit=true.
Persistent tool-approval updates are owned by the scheduler's updatePolicy path; onConfirm callbacks no longer publish UPDATE_POLICY.
Tool invocation errors normalize through ToolExecutor.execute, mapping thrown errors to ToolErrorType.UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION and ToolResult.error fields to their declared type.
Confirmation requests correlate via MessageBus IDs; a 30-second timeout resolves to ask_user and abort resolves to deny.
MCP output content blocks (text/image/audio/resource/resource_link) are transformed into GenAI Part[] with inlineData for binary content; unknown blocks are dropped.
Legacy tool-name aliases are normalized at getTool lookup and expanded in excludeTools so policy targets both the old and new name.

contradictions.description: Two MCP discovery drivers with divergent lifecycles: McpClient.discoverInto (managed by McpClientManager) and exported connectAndDiscover both exist and both throw on empty discovery.
DiscoveredMCPToolInvocation.allowlist is a static per-process Set that parallels the persistent policy engine's approvals.

respectsAutoEdit=true is only set by EditTool and WriteFileTool invocations; other Kind.Edit tools (e.g. tracker tools) don't use the AUTO_EDIT fast-path. AUTO_EDIT scope is therefore narrower than ApprovalMode documentation implies.
DiscoveredToolInvocation treats any non-empty stderr as a tool error, even with exit code 0.
generateValidName truncation (first30 + '...' + last30) can collide distinct MCP tool names; registerTool silently overwrites the earlier entry.
mcp-client.ts is 2151 lines, exceeding the 1500-line reading-budget guideline and concentrating OAuth/transport/discovery in one file.
DiscoveredMCPToolInvocation.allowlist uses dotted server.tool keys while policy updates flow with the underscore-separated mcp_server_tool convention.

risks.description: Tool-discovery command output is parsed with minimal validation (three accepted shapes, no schema check), so malformed external discovery can register broken tools.
risks.suggestedGuard: Validate declarations with SchemaValidator and drop invalid entries with a diagnostic.

risks.description: MCP name truncation can collide two distinct server+tool pairs; registerTool overwrites without error.
risks.suggestedGuard: Append a short stable hash suffix to truncated names.

risks.description: Confirmation-bus 30s timeout resolves to ask_user; a lost response or non-interactive driver can stall or mis-route.
risks.suggestedGuard: Make the timeout configurable and error out in non-interactive drivers.

risks.description: DiscoveredToolInvocation treats any stderr as an error; valid external tools that log progress to stderr report as failed to the model.
risks.suggestedGuard: Treat non-empty stderr as warnings when exit code is 0; surface stderr via data field.

risks.description: Static in-memory MCP allowlist can drift from the persistent policy engine across long-running sessions.
risks.suggestedGuard: Consolidate session-scoped MCP approvals under the policy engine.

risks.description: Plan-mode wording is patched into declarations by string concatenation at declaration time; upstream base-description changes can read oddly.
risks.suggestedGuard: Move plan-mode wording into tool definitions and select a variant instead of string patching.

risks.description: MCP transport fallback (HTTP -> SSE -> OAuth) can emit confusing error text because only the last attempt's error is surfaced.
risks.suggestedGuard: Aggregate per-transport attempts into a single error with breadcrumbs.

risks.description: mcp-client.ts at 2151 lines increases review friction; changes to OAuth, transport, and discovery share a file and diff-review locality.

observabilitySignals: coreEvents.emitMcpProgress({ serverName, callId, progressToken, progress, total, message })
debugLogger.warn/log/error for registration overrides, discovery outcomes, transport attempts
runInDevTraceSpan({ operation: GeminiCliOperation.ToolCall, … }) with GEN_AI_TOOL_NAME / GEN_AI_TOOL_CALL_ID attributes
ToolOutputTruncatedEvent emitted via logToolOutputTruncated when output exceeds char budgets
gaps: No test for discovered-tool malformed-JSON declarations.
No test for generateValidName truncation collisions.
No test for confirmation-bus 30s timeout outcome.
No test for cross-session behavior of DiscoveredMCPToolInvocation.allowlist.
No integration test asserting ALL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES matches Config.createToolRegistry's registered set.

openQuestions: Why maintain a per-process MCP allowlist in mcp-tool.ts when the policy engine already persists approvals?
What is the intended behavior when tool-call-command is unset but tool-discovery-command returns DiscoveredTool entries?
Is the static allowlist in DiscoveredMCPToolInvocation intentionally un-cleared across tests?
Should generateValidName retain a deterministic hash suffix to avoid truncation collisions?
Is mcp-client.ts's exported connectAndDiscover public SDK surface or dead code relative to the manager lifecycle?
Should discovered-tool stderr-only output be a warning rather than an error?
